verdict.rationale: Working Copy documents SSH as a Git transport. Private keys can be imported or generated in-app, can live on the Secure Enclave, and SSH commands can list repositories on Linux, BSD or Synology servers. So it connects to remote servers over SSH with key authentication, but only for Git operations, and the docs never name supported key algorithms. missing for 10: explicit Ed25519/ECDSA/RSA key-type support, general (non-Git) SSH or terminal sessions to remote servers, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect to remote servers using SSH with Ed25519, ECDSA, or RSA keys

citations.quote: Working Copy supports https, ssh, git, and http protocols.
You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
configure a regular Linux server, BSD server & Synology NAS to act as a hosting provider, using SSH commands for listing repositories.
